title: Make 'athena land --pr' work on squash-only repositories
summary: Athena will read the repository's allowed merge methods from GitHub and request an allowed one (squash when it is the only one, with the job's trailers in the last paragraph and one Athena-Job). After a squash lands, Athena rebuilds the local branch onto main, replaying later landed jobs and records without losing unlanded work. The merge-commit decision from job 9h2j in docs/decisions.md and the design doc is revised, citing Sri's choice.

defaults_applied.how: New tests use a real temporary local git repository; cargo test and clippy must pass.
Behavior criteria name the cargo commands the verifier runs.
The fix targets broken ancestry after a squash, not the single PR #40 instance.
Docs and commit text are written for an outside reader.
The decision revision cites Sri's choice and the host's reported flags.
One change, limited to merge method selection, squash message, local resync and the docs.

assumptions: Method preference order when several are allowed is merge, then squash, then rebase, which keeps today's behavior on repositories that allow merge commits.
Allowed methods come from GET repos/{owner}/{name} (allow_merge_commit, allow_squash_merge, allow_rebase_merge) through the PrHost trait in crates/athena-core/src/gh.rs.
The squash commit message is supplied to the merge call as commit_title and commit_message, built from the job's trailers.
Local rebuild after a squash lands is done in the landing flow (athena-core/athena-gate/athena-git), reusing the existing squash-chain machinery in docs/design/squash-chain-landing.md where it fits.
The 'design doc' to revise is docs/design/native-pr-landing.md, which records the merge-commit landing decision; the decision entry is the one near line 1901 of docs/decisions.md.
Sri's choice is cited by name as the owner's decision, with no personal data such as an email address.

acceptance_criteria.text: The host client reads allow_merge_commit, allow_squash_merge and allow_rebase_merge, and merge requests an allowed method. With only squash allowed it sends merge_method=squash, and with none allowed it fails with a clear error. Check with cargo test -p athena-core.

A squash commit message ends with a last paragraph holding the job's trailers with exactly one Athena-Job line. A test builds a squash on a real local git repository and shows that the history check passes on main. Check with cargo test.

A test on a real temporary git repository simulates a squash landing. It then shows that the local branch is rebuilt on the squash commit, that the later landed jobs and records are kept, that unlanded work is not lost, and that the next PR branch merges with main without conflict. Check with cargo test.
cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo fmt --check all pass.

docs/decisions.md has a new or revised entry superseding the 9h2j merge-commit landing decision. It cites Sri's choice of squash-only support over enabling merge commits, and it states the host's reported flags.

The design doc (docs/design/native-pr-landing.md) is updated to describe method discovery, the squash message format and the post-squash resync, and no longer says that PRs always land as merge commits.
CHANGELOG.md notes the change. No governance or records files change.

out_of_scope: Enabling merge commits or changing the repository's settings on the host.
Support for hosts other than github.com.
Rewriting the PR #40 history or any records.
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml, CI workflows or lint configuration.
departures: Higher cost and time than the reference: the request has three parts, touches several crates, and needs real-git tests for the squash resync, which is the hard part. I lowered the verification probability for the same reason.
